title: Left-handed dental operatory: both stools and the cart in the mirrored clock zones
instruction: Set up this dental surgery for the next patient. The patient will lie in the chair with their head on the headrest and mouth at the painted mark. Today's dentist is left-handed and works four-handed with a chairside assistant. Put the dentist's stool (blue), the assistant's stool (green, the taller one) and the assistant's mobile cart (grey) where they go around the chair for this dentist and assistant, each standing upright on the floor, not on the chair, then let go of them.
context: Dental assistants (O*NET 31-9091.00) set up the operatory before each patient. Four-handed dentistry places the team by the clock concept (zones of activity): seen from above with the patient's face as the clock and the top of the head at 12, a right-handed dentist works at 7 to 12, the assistant sits at 2 to 4, instruments pass over the chest in the transfer zone at 4 to 7 and the static zone at 12 to 2 holds the set-up. For a left-handed dentist every zone mirrors about the 12 to 6 axis: operator 12 to 5, transfer 5 to 8, assistant 8 to 10, static 10 to 12. The assistant sits higher than the dentist, so the assistant's stool is the taller one, and nothing stands in the transfer zone. Sources differ on whether the mobile cart goes in the assistant's or the static zone, so either counts. Setting the usual right-handed layout from habit is the error this checks: the dentist would have to work across the patient.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and is the surgery's floor. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A table-top model of a dental surgery; six things are on the table. (1) Patient chair: a light blue painted MDF block 80 mm (along x) by 300 mm (along y) by 40 mm tall, fixed to the table, x 22.0 to 30.0 cm, y +7.0 to +37.0 cm. (2) Headrest: a light blue painted MDF block 60 mm (x) by 50 mm (y) by 40 mm tall, fixed to the table against the chair's -y end, x 23.0 to 29.0 cm, y +2.0 to +7.0 cm. A patient lying face up in the chair has the head on the headrest, the top of the head toward -y and the feet toward +y, so the patient's left is -x (toward the arm bases) and the right is +x. (3) Mouth mark: a red painted disc 12 mm across on the headrest's top, centred at x 26.0 cm, y +5.0 cm. (4) Dentist's stool: a loose blue cylinder 50 mm across and 40 mm tall, 120 g (3D-printed PLA, weighted with steel shot), both ends alike, standing on the floor centred at x 28.0 cm, y -33.0 cm. (5) Assistant's stool: a loose green cylinder 50 mm across and 60 mm tall, 150 g (the same material), both ends alike, standing beyond the foot of the chair centred at x 40.0 cm, y +33.0 cm. (6) Assistant's mobile cart: a loose grey box 60 mm (along x) by 45 mm (along y) by 45 mm tall, 200 g (3D-printed PLA, weighted with steel shot), standing on the floor centred at x 36.0 cm, y -34.0 cm with its sides square to the table. Clock positions are seen from above round the mouth mark: 12 o'clock toward -y (behind the head), 3 toward -x (the patient's left), 6 toward +y (the feet), 9 toward +x (the patient's right). At the start the dentist's stool is at 11:54 and 381 mm from the mouth, the cart at 11:31 and 403 mm, the assistant's stool at 6:53 and 313 mm: all more than 200 mm away. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the three objects' poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a top photo with a protractor centred on the mouth mark, and a ruler). Clock angle: seen from above round the mouth mark's centre, clockwise from 12 o'clock (-y, behind the head), 30 degrees per hour; 3 o'clock is -x, the patient's left. Distance: horizontal, from the mouth mark's centre to the object's centre. An object is in a window when it stands (its vertical axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either end up, its lowest point within 5 mm of the floor: not on the chair, on another object or held up) with its centre 80 to 200 mm from the mouth at a clock angle inside the window. Windows, inside every source's zone limits: left-handed dentist's stool 12:30 to 3:30 (operator zone 12 to 5); left-handed assistant's stool 8:15 to 9:45 (assistant zone 8 to 10); cart 8:15 to 11:45 (the left-handed assistant's side, assistant or static zone, 8 to 12); right-handed dentist's stool 8:30 to 11:30 and assistant's stool 2:15 to 3:45. Released: at no step of the last 0.5 s was a gripper's pad-tip point (midway between its finger tips) less than 10 mm above the object's top while within finger reach of its centre (the widest over every yaw: 90 mm from a stool's centre and 103 mm from the cart's with the fingers fully open, 52 and 65 mm closed). Settled: its centre moved under 2 mm in all over the last 0.5 s. Decision list, first match wins: (1) any object not released or not settled, or any object's centre within 200 mm of the mouth at 5 to 8 o'clock (the left-handed transfer zone, over the chest): 0. (2) Dentist's stool, assistant's stool and cart each in their left-handed windows, every object settled in each of the last two 0.5 s (still for 1 s): 1.0. (3) Both stools in their left-handed windows: 0.75. (4) The dentist's stool in its left-handed window, the assistant's stool not in its: 0.5. (5) The right-handed layout, dentist's stool 8:30 to 11:30 and assistant's stool 2:15 to 3:45: 0.25. (6) Anything else: 0. Every outcome: dentist's stool at 1:30 and assistant's at 9:00, both 100 mm out, cart at 11:00, 130 mm out: 1.0; the same with the cart left at its start or set behind the head at 12:30 (the right-handed static zone): 0.75; the assistant's stool left at its start or set at 3:00: 0.5; the textbook right-handed layout (dentist's stool at 11:00, assistant's at 3:00): 0.25; the stools swapped (dentist's at 9:00, assistant's at 2:00): 0; the cart or a stool at 7:00, 150 mm out (transfer zone): 0; a stool on the chair, tipped over, still gripped or still moving: 0; nothing moved: 0. Run limit 1,200 steps (1 minute at 20 Hz); the run ends early once 1.0 has held for 2 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. The surgery is a table-top model: the chair is a fixed block with a headrest and a painted mouth mark, the stools are cylinders and the cart a box, and the light, delivery unit and suction are left out. Distances are scaled down (the stools end 100 mm from the mouth); the clock zones are angles, which the scaling keeps, so the task tests the real decision. The grippers are read only to check each object was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the dentist's stool upright centred at x 28.0 cm, y -33.0 cm, the assistant's stool centred at x 40.0 cm, y +33.0 cm and the cart centred at x 36.0 cm, y -34.0 cm with its sides square to the table. The chair, headrest and mouth mark are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
scores: Dream-1 run: not scored (the policy declined the instruction as unsafe, reading it as dropping objects off the table onto the floor, so the trial errored before any action); demo: 1.0
